boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain United States Naval Academy
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe Annapolis food destinations with directly verified late hours. Confirm availability before leaving, especially on holidays.

cards.title: Naz's Halal Food
cards.subtitle: 2510 Riva Road, Suite A101, Annapolis
cards.notes: Use the official ordering page to check the day’s schedule, then choose pickup or delivery from this Annapolis halal-food location.
cards.short_summary: A late-running halal-food option on Riva Road.
cards.evidence_claim: Naz's lists Annapolis hours through 2 AM Sunday–Thursday and through 4 AM Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official hours: 10:30 AM–2 AM Sunday–Thursday; 10:30 AM–4 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Pizza Boli's
cards.subtitle: 1900 Forest Drive, Annapolis
cards.notes: Check the location’s ordering page before heading out; it identifies this Forest Drive shop and its late pickup and delivery hours.
cards.short_summary: A pizza carryout and delivery stop with weekend hours to 2 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Boli's lists the Annapolis location open until 1 AM Monday–Thursday and Sunday, and until 2 AM Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official hours: 10 AM–1 AM Monday–Thursday and Sunday; 10 AM–2 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Domino's on Bay Ridge Road
cards.subtitle: 914 Bay Ridge Road, Annapolis
cards.notes: Place a carryout or delivery order through the official location page and recheck the posted close time before departing.
cards.short_summary: A Bay Ridge Road pizza option listed through midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino's official Annapolis page for 914 Bay Ridge Road lists the store open until 12 AM.
cards.source_title: Domino's Pizza at 914 Bay Ridge Road
cards.access_notes: Official location page currently displays an open-until time of 12 AM; verify the day-specific status when ordering.

cards.title: Domino's at Forest Plaza
cards.subtitle: 77 Forest Plaza, Annapolis
cards.notes: Use the official store page for carryout or delivery and confirm the listed hours before making the Forest Plaza run.
cards.short_summary: A second Annapolis Domino's location listed through midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino's official Annapolis page for 77 Forest Plaza lists the store open until 12 AM.
cards.access_notes: Official location page currently displays an open-until time of 12 AM; verify the day-specific status when ordering.

cards.title: McDonald's on West Street
cards.subtitle: 1941 West Street, Annapolis
cards.notes: For a drive-thru stop, use the official location page or mobile ordering; lobby and drive-thru hours are listed separately.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour drive-thru on West Street.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald's lists this Annapolis drive-thru as open 24 hours daily; its lobby is listed until 11 PM.
cards.access_notes: Official listing: drive-thru open 24 hours daily; restaurant/lobby 6 AM–11 PM daily.

cards.title: Taco Bell on West Street
cards.subtitle: 1803 West Street, Annapolis
cards.notes: Order ahead or use the drive-thru, and consult the official location page for the current day’s late-night operating window.
cards.short_summary: A West Street taco stop with posted 1–2 AM closes.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell's Annapolis location lists hours until 1 AM Sunday–Thursday and until 2 AM Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official location listing: 9 AM–1 AM Sunday–Thursday; 9 AM–2 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Wendy's on West Street
cards.subtitle: 1949 West Street, Annapolis
cards.notes: Check the official location listing immediately before leaving, then use the posted restaurant service options for your order.
cards.short_summary: A West Street fast-food location listed to close at 3:59 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy's official Annapolis directory lists the 1949 West Street location open until 3:59 AM.
cards.access_notes: Official Annapolis directory currently lists this location with a 3:59 AM closing time; verify hours before travel.

cards.title: El Toro Bravo Mexican
cards.subtitle: Annapolis, Maryland
cards.notes: Check the restaurant’s official site for the operating day, then plan an early late-night pickup when Friday hours extend later.
cards.short_summary: A Mexican restaurant with Friday service posted to 2 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: El Toro Bravo's official site lists Friday hours from 11 AM to 2 AM.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Friday hours of 11 AM–2 AM; check the site for current hours on other days.

cards.title: Broadneck Grill & Cantina
cards.subtitle: 1364 Cape Saint Claire Road, Annapolis
cards.notes: Use the official directions and hours page to confirm service, particularly if relying on its separately listed late-night menu.
cards.short_summary: A Cape Saint Claire Road restaurant with a late-night menu.
cards.evidence_claim: Broadneck Grill & Cantina lists hours until 2 AM daily and states that a late-night menu is available until closing.
cards.source_title: Broadneck Grill & Cantina directions and hours
cards.access_notes: Official page lists 2 AM closing daily; it specifies a late-night menu until close after the main kitchen closes.

cards.entity_name: Ports of Call at DoubleTree Annapolis
cards.title: Ports of Call
cards.subtitle: 210 Holiday Court, Annapolis
cards.notes: Check the hotel’s dining page before leaving and use the Friday or Saturday dinner window when the restaurant is posted latest.
cards.short_summary: A hotel restaurant with Friday and Saturday hours to 2 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: DoubleTree Annapolis lists Ports of Call open until 2 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Ports of Call at DoubleTree Annapolis
cards.access_notes: Official hotel dining page lists weekday hours to 12 AM and Friday–Saturday hours from 5 PM–2 AM.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Academy spaces with documented academic, collaboration, recreation, or team uses.

cards.title: Nimitz Library
cards.subtitle: Academic spaces and services for the Naval Academy community
cards.notes: Start at the library when you need a change of working pace; its four floors include tables, carrels, lounge seating, standing tables, and computers.
cards.short_summary: A multi-floor campus base for individual work, group work, and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: Nimitz Library provides spaces, services, and resources for the Naval Academy community, including a variety of study settings across four floors.
cards.access_notes: Library services are primarily for the Academy community; authorized researchers and other users have specified access circumstances.

cards.title: Nautilus Room
cards.subtitle: Nimitz Library main floor
cards.notes: Check the posted schedule before settling in; when it is not needed for library instruction, use this classroom for individual or group study.
cards.short_summary: A library classroom that can double as a study setting between scheduled uses.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nautilus Room is a Nimitz Library classroom available for individual or group study when it is not in use for another purpose.
cards.access_notes: Library classes, meetings, and events take priority; consult the schedule posted on or near the door.

cards.title: Nimitz Room 227
cards.subtitle: Nimitz Library second floor
cards.notes: Use the room for a focused solo or small-group session when no library class or meeting has it scheduled; look for the nearby room schedule.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor library classroom used as an open lab outside instructional commitments.
cards.evidence_claim: Nimitz 227 serves as an open lab and is available for individual or group study when it is not in use for library instruction or other priority activity.
cards.access_notes: Library instruction has first priority; use depends on the room schedule.

cards.title: Nimitz Room 301
cards.subtitle: Nimitz Library third floor
cards.notes: Reserve this eight-person room for a planned team session and use its whiteboard and screen to keep the work visible to everyone.
cards.short_summary: A reservable third-floor group room with presentation and whiteboard tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Nimitz Room 301 is a reservable third-floor study room for eight people with a whiteboard, screen, and VHS/DVD player.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the library's room-reservation system; reservations are intended for occasional use.

cards.title: Nimitz Room 302
cards.subtitle: Nimitz Library third floor
cards.notes: Book this four-person room when a smaller group needs a contained workspace; bring material that benefits from its whiteboard or chalkboard.
cards.short_summary: A compact reservable room for small-group work on the library's third floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Nimitz Room 302 is a reservable third-floor study room for four people with a whiteboard, chalkboard, and white-noise machine.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the library's room-reservation system; availability varies by time slot.

cards.title: Halsey Field House
cards.subtitle: Indoor athletics and physical-fitness facility
cards.notes: Use the facility only during its posted operating times and authorized activities; its documented amenities include courts, squash, weight training, and a climbing wall.
cards.short_summary: An indoor athletics building supporting several forms of physical activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Halsey Field House includes an indoor football practice facility, basketball courts, international squash courts, weight-training facilities, and a climbing wall.
cards.source_title: Athletics | The Blue and Gold Book | USNA
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to posted facility hours and Academy authorization; midshipmen have priority in athletic facilities.

cards.title: Lejeune Hall
cards.subtitle: Aquatics, wrestling, and conditioning facility
cards.notes: Plan an authorized workout around the facility schedule; Lejeune combines an Olympic-sized pool, diving facilities, wrestling space, and conditioning areas.
cards.short_summary: A named athletic building centered on aquatics, wrestling, and conditioning.
cards.evidence_claim: Lejeune Hall contains an Olympic-sized pool, diving platforms and tank, a wrestling arena, and personal conditioning areas.
cards.source_title: Athletics | The Blue and Gold Book | USNA
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to posted facility hours and Academy authorization; midshipmen have priority in athletic facilities.

cards.title: Macdonough Hall
cards.subtitle: Multi-sport physical education and athletics building
cards.notes: Coordinate activity with Academy access rules; this hall brings together gymnastics, boxing, volleyball, aquatics, racquet sports, basketball, and conditioning facilities.
cards.short_summary: A multi-use athletics building with a broad mix of documented activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Macdonough Hall has facilities for gymnastics, boxing, volleyball, swimming, water polo, racquetball, basketball, and personal conditioning.
cards.source_title: Athletics | The Blue and Gold Book | USNA
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to posted facility hours and Academy authorization; midshipmen have priority in athletic facilities.

cards.title: Wesley Brown Field House
cards.subtitle: Physical education, varsity athletics, club sports, and fitness
cards.notes: Look to the scheduled program or authorized club activity before entering; the building is designated for physical education, varsity athletics, club sports, and personal fitness.
cards.short_summary: A large Academy field house serving structured athletics and fitness programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wesley Brown Field House houses facilities for physical education, varsity athletics, club sports, and personal fitness.
cards.source_title: Athletics | The Blue and Gold Book | USNA
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to posted facility hours and Academy authorization; midshipmen have priority in athletic facilities.

cards.title: Hubbard Hall
cards.subtitle: Home of Navy crew and the Fisher Rowing Center
cards.notes: View this waterfront athletics landmark from authorized areas, or participate only through scheduled rowing activity; it houses the Academy's crew squads and rowing center.
cards.short_summary: A named home base for Academy crew programs on the waterfront.
cards.evidence_claim: Hubbard Hall is the home for Navy's crew squads and includes the Fisher Rowing Center.
cards.source_title: Athletics | The Blue and Gold Book | USNA
cards.access_notes: Participation and building access are subject to Academy authorization and scheduled program requirements.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission activities at the Academy and in Annapolis, with access details from official public sources.

cards.title: Browse the Naval Academy Museum
cards.subtitle: Preble Hall, U.S. Naval Academy
cards.notes: Walk through Preble Hall’s naval-history exhibits together, then leave time to look closely at the ship models and artifacts.
cards.short_summary: A free museum stop on the Yard with clearly stated visitor access.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA states that the U.S. Naval Academy Museum is free and ADA accessible.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit — U.S. Naval Academy Museum
cards.access_notes: General public pedestrian access is through Gate 1 or Gate 8; visitors 18+ need valid photo ID. Check museum hours and federal-holiday closures before going.

cards.entity_name: U.S. Naval Academy Cemetery and Columbarium
cards.title: Visit the Cemetery and Columbarium
cards.subtitle: Hospital Point, U.S. Naval Academy
cards.notes: Take the mile walk from the Visitor Center to read memorials and use the locator kiosk for a quiet, respectful history stop.
cards.short_summary: A public visitation site on the Academy grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA says the Cemetery and Columbarium are open to public visitation and open for visitation from sunrise to sunset.
cards.access_notes: Enter through the Visitor Access Center with government-issued Real ID and follow cemetery rules; recreational walking, eating, drinking, biking, and jogging are prohibited there.

cards.title: Attend a public chapel service
cards.subtitle: U.S. Naval Academy Main Chapel
cards.notes: Choose a listed service and attend with friends, allowing extra time for the Gate 1 pedestrian security process and photo-ID check.
cards.short_summary: Public chapel services provide a no-cost, scheduled way to experience the Yard.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA says its Chaplain’s Center holds services open to the public and that public events are free unless otherwise noted.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the service schedule before traveling. Gate access rules apply; visitors 18+ must carry valid photo identification.

cards.title: See Maryland Black-history exhibits
cards.subtitle: 84 Franklin Street, Annapolis
cards.notes: Meet at the museum and move through the exhibits at your own pace, pausing to compare the stories and objects that stand out.
cards.short_summary: Maryland’s official African American heritage museum has free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Annapolis identifies the Banneker-Douglass Museum at 84 Franklin Street and states that admission is free, with donations encouraged.
cards.source_title: A History Lover’s Itinerary — Visit Annapolis
cards.access_notes: The cited visitor information lists Tuesday–Saturday hours; verify current hours with the museum before your visit.

cards.title: Walk the Waterworks Park trails
cards.subtitle: 260 Defense Highway, Annapolis
cards.notes: Bring a friend for the park’s hiking paths, then settle at the picnic area or benches to watch the water and wildlife.
cards.short_summary: A 40-acre city recreation area for a low-key outdoor hang.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Annapolis states Waterworks Park is free of charge, requires no permits, and offers hiking trails, picnic places, and fishing.
cards.access_notes: Use the address provided by the City and follow posted park rules. Any transport or optional equipment is separate from park access.

cards.title: Read the Kunta Kinte-Alex Haley Memorial
cards.subtitle: City Dock, historic Annapolis
cards.notes: Start at the sculpture group, then follow the ten Story Wall markers and finish at the Compass Rose across from Market House.
cards.short_summary: A City Dock memorial with multiple interpretive elements to explore together.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes the memorial’s sculpture group, ten Story Wall markers, and Compass Rose at City Dock.
cards.source_title: About the Memorial — City of Annapolis
cards.access_notes: The memorial is in a City of Annapolis waterfront park; the City’s public-water-access report states all City waterfront parks are free to access.

cards.title: Pause by the waterfront at Susan Campbell Park
cards.subtitle: City Dock, Annapolis
cards.notes: Use the park as a meet-up point for a waterside conversation, then stroll the nearby public dock area without booking an activity.
cards.short_summary: A named City Dock waterfront park for a simple outdoor meet-up.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s City Dock plan identifies Susan Campbell Park as a public recreational space at the waterfront.
cards.source_title: Annapolis City Dock Master Plan — City of Annapolis
cards.access_notes: The City’s public-water-access report states all City of Annapolis waterfront parks are free to access. Parking and boat services may cost extra.

cards.entity_name: Ellen O. Moyer Nature Park at Back Creek
cards.title: Take the Back Creek nature loop
cards.subtitle: Edgewood Road, Annapolis
cards.notes: Walk the park’s trail with a friend, use the benches or pavilion for a break, and keep the visit focused on the natural area.
cards.short_summary: A city nature park with trail and water-access amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s parks listing identifies Ellen O. Moyer Nature Park at Back Creek and lists a bike/hike trail, nature area, pavilion, benches, and water access.
cards.source_title: Amenities at Parks, Trails and Playgrounds — City of Annapolis
cards.access_notes: The City’s public-water-access report states all City waterfront parks are free to access. Use only designated paths and follow posted conditions.

cards.title: Meet up at Carr’s/Elktonia Heritage Park
cards.subtitle: Bembe Beach Road, Annapolis
cards.notes: Plan a daylight waterfront meet-up, then explore the adjacent public park setting and talk through the site’s local cultural history.
cards.short_summary: A named city waterfront park beside the Annapolis Maritime Museum campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Carr’s/Elktonia Heritage Park on Bembe Beach Road as a location for a free, public 2026 Juneteenth celebration.
cards.source_title: Annapolis Juneteenth Celebration Press Release — City of Annapolis
cards.access_notes: The City’s public-water-access report states all City waterfront parks are free to access. Check City notices for any event-related closures or parking limits.

cards.title: Do a State House self-guided visit
cards.subtitle: 100 State Circle, Annapolis
cards.notes: Pick up the self-guided material by the first-floor Archives Room, then compare the building’s historic rooms and civic displays together.
cards.short_summary: A public state building with self-guided visitor information on site.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryland State Archives states that the Maryland State House is open to the public daily and that self-guided tour information is available on the first floor.
cards.source_title: Maryland State House Tours — Maryland State Archives
cards.access_notes: Open 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m. except Christmas and New Year’s Day according to the State Archives; picture ID and metal-detector screening are required.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten documented stops around City Dock, Main Street, Pinkney Street, State Circle, East Street, and Prince George Street just beyond the Academy’s historic-district edge.

cards.title: Museum of Historic Annapolis
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor · 99 Main Street
cards.notes: Start at the Main Street museum to orient your walk with the chronological Annapolis: An American Story exhibition.
cards.short_summary: A documented 400-year introduction to the city.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Annapolis identifies 99 Main Street as the Museum of Historic Annapolis, home to the chronological Annapolis: An American Story exhibition.
cards.access_notes: Check the museum’s current visitor information before going.

cards.title: William Paca House and Garden
cards.subtitle: Prince George Street corridor · 186 Prince George Street
cards.notes: Walk Prince George Street for the restored Georgian house and terraced garden; choose garden entry or a guided house tour.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark with a two-acre restored garden.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Annapolis documents the 1760s William Paca House as a National Historic Landmark and describes its restored two-acre garden.
cards.access_notes: Hours and admission vary by season; the official page lists current schedules and entry options.

cards.title: Hogshead Trades Museum
cards.subtitle: Pinkney Street corridor · 43 Pinkney Street
cards.notes: Use Pinkney Street for a compact living-history stop focused on working-class Annapolitans and hands-on trade interpretation.
cards.short_summary: A rare surviving working-class 18th-century building.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Annapolis calls Hogshead Annapolis’s only living-history museum and a rare surviving example of a common 18th-century building type.
cards.access_notes: Confirm opening times with Historic Annapolis; the building requires stairs for entry and interior access.

cards.title: Waterfront Warehouse
cards.subtitle: Pinkney Street corridor · 4 Pinkney Street
cards.notes: Continue down Pinkney Street to see the waterfront warehouse and its model of late-18th-century Annapolis.
cards.short_summary: A small surviving 18th-century waterfront warehouse.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Annapolis describes the Waterfront Warehouse as a rare surviving small Annapolis waterfront warehouse from the 18th century with a period city model.
cards.access_notes: Historic Annapolis notes two steps at entry and no restrooms on site.

cards.title: Kunta Kinte-Alex Haley Memorial
cards.subtitle: City Dock corridor · beside Market House Plaza
cards.notes: Pause at City Dock to read the memorial’s family-history and reconciliation themes before continuing along the waterfront.
cards.short_summary: A City Dock memorial centered on heritage and reconciliation.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Annapolis states that the City Dock memorial conveys Alex Haley’s vision for racial reconciliation and honors family history and cultural heritage.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor memorial at City Dock; observe it respectfully and follow any posted waterfront conditions.

cards.title: Compass Rose
cards.subtitle: City Dock corridor · Market House Plaza
cards.notes: Find the bronze-and-granite Compass Rose in Market House Plaza as a quick public-art stop beside the dock.
cards.short_summary: A documented sculpture in the City Dock plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Annapolis sculpture-tour map places the bronze-and-granite Compass Rose in Market House Plaza.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public artwork in Market House Plaza.

cards.title: John Shaw House
cards.subtitle: State Circle corridor · 21 State Circle
cards.notes: Circle State Circle to view the former home of cabinetmaker John Shaw, a named landmark at the Main Street end.
cards.short_summary: The oldest building on State Circle.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Annapolis identifies the John Shaw House at 21 State Circle as the oldest building on the circle and notes Shaw occupied it from 1784.
cards.access_notes: Historic Annapolis states that the Shaw House is not currently open to the public; view from public streets only.

cards.title: James Brice House
cards.subtitle: East Street corridor · 42 East Street
cards.notes: Take East Street past the James Brice House to see one of the city’s largest surviving colonial-era homes.
cards.short_summary: A major surviving colonial Annapolis house.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Annapolis describes the James Brice House at 42 East Street as one of Annapolis’s largest and most elegant historic homes.
cards.access_notes: Historic Annapolis states that the house is not currently open during restoration; view from public streets only.

cards.title: Shiplap House
cards.subtitle: Pinkney Street corridor · 18 Pinkney Street
cards.notes: Notice the overlapping-board siding on Pinkney Street and use it to spot this early Annapolis frame house from outside.
cards.short_summary: A named early frame house defined by its shiplap siding.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Annapolis identifies Shiplap House at 18 Pinkney Street as one of the oldest surviving frame houses in Annapolis and explains its name.
cards.access_notes: Historic Annapolis lists the building as administrative offices and not open to the public; view from the street.

cards.title: Market House
cards.subtitle: City Dock corridor · Market House Plaza
cards.notes: Use Market House as your City Dock landmark, then pair it with the nearby memorial and Compass Rose on the plaza.
cards.short_summary: A central City Dock reference point in the civic art map.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Annapolis identifies the Compass Rose as situated next to the Market House and across from the Kunta Kinte-Alex Haley Memorial.
cards.access_notes: Use public plaza and sidewalk areas; individual Market House tenant access may vary.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented U.S. Naval Academy ceremonies and customs spanning plebe year, class identity, military pageantry, and the Army–Navy rivalry.

cards.title: Trade the Dixie Cup for a Cover
cards.subtitle: Plebe-year culmination at Herndon Monument
cards.notes: Use the official history and event photography to understand the teamwork ritual; do not attempt to climb the monument outside the Academy’s organized event.
cards.short_summary: Plebes form a human pyramid to replace the hat atop Herndon Monument.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA identifies the Herndon Monument Climb as the traditional culmination of plebe year, in which plebes replace the monument’s “dixie cup” with an upperclassman’s cover.
cards.source_title: History and Traditions of the Herndon Monument Climb
cards.access_notes: Participation is an Academy-organized plebe event; follow current USNA access and event guidance.

cards.title: The Plebe-Year Stress Test
cards.subtitle: Upperclass-led plebe rite of passage
cards.notes: Read the Academy’s event account for context on this structured training milestone; it is not a visitor activity or self-directed challenge.
cards.short_summary: A formal physical and mental challenge marks the plebe class’s progression.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA describes Sea Trials as an upperclass-led final physical and mental challenge for plebes that tests teamwork and cements company and class bonds.
cards.source_title: Naval Academy to Hold Herndon Climb on May 17
cards.access_notes: Restricted to the plebe class and conducted under Academy supervision.

cards.title: Baptize the Class Ring
cards.subtitle: Commissioning Week class-ring ceremony
cards.notes: See the official Commissioning Week history for the ring-dipping custom and its class-designed crests; attendance details vary by year.
cards.short_summary: Juniors first wear their class rings after a ceremonial Seven Seas water dip.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA states that second-class midshipmen do not wear their class rings until they are “baptized” at Ring Dance, a Commissioning Week tradition since 1925.
cards.access_notes: A class event; consult current Commissioning Week information for any viewing arrangements.

cards.title: Melted Rings, Linked Classes
cards.subtitle: Memorial Hall alumni-to-midshipman ceremony
cards.notes: Look for official ceremony images and ring displays to trace the fifty-year class connection, rather than treating the rings as ordinary souvenirs.
cards.short_summary: Alumni rings are incorporated into the gold for a linked midshipman class.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA reports that Bonds of Gold includes alumni class rings and miniatures being donated, melted down, and included in the gold for the linked midshipman class’s rings.
cards.source_title: Bonds of Gold Ceremony Connects Classes of 1967 and 2017
cards.access_notes: Ceremony participation is organized by USNA and its alumni link program.

cards.title: Award the Color Company Pennant
cards.subtitle: Worden Field company-recognition parade
cards.notes: Follow current USNA parade notices if you want to watch the formal presentation; respect posted entry, seating, and security directions.
cards.short_summary: The Academy recognizes a company’s semester-long performance with a pennant ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA says the Color Parade’s highlight is presentation of the color company pennant to the company selected for excellence in academics, athletics, and professional accomplishments.
cards.source_title: 2025 May Events Open to the Public and Road/Bridge Closures
cards.access_notes: USNA’s 2025 notice listed the event on Worden Field; future access and timing must be confirmed with current notices.

cards.title: March from Bancroft to Worden
cards.subtitle: Brigade military pageantry on Worden Field
cards.notes: Check the current official parade schedule before visiting, then watch the march, manual of arms, honors, and pass-in-review from authorized areas.
cards.short_summary: The Brigade’s recurring formal parades make military training visible on the Yard.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA states that formal dress parades have been part of Naval Academy training since 1845 and describes the Brigade’s march to Worden Field, manual of arms, honors, and review.
cards.access_notes: Use current USNA announcements for parade dates, gate procedures, and visitor access.

cards.title: Take the Honor Oath, Receive a Coin
cards.subtitle: Fifty-year link class ceremony
cards.notes: Treat this as an honor-program ceremony: use the official account to understand the oath and coin’s purpose, not as an unsupervised reenactment.
cards.short_summary: A linked alumni class presents coins after midshipmen take the honor oath.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA reports that at the Honor Coin Ceremony, midshipmen take the honor oath and receive a coin made by their 50-year link class as a reminder of the honor concept.
cards.access_notes: An Academy and alumni-link program event, not a general visitor activity.

cards.title: The Third-Class “Youngster Luau”
cards.subtitle: Class tradition within the alumni-link program
cards.notes: Use the Academy’s alumni-link overview to place this named class event in the midshipman calendar; participation is organized internally.
cards.short_summary: A named third-class gathering is part of USNA’s documented class-event cycle.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA lists the Youngster Luau among the events in its Another Link in the Chain program, which the article describes as honoring Naval Academy history and traditions.
cards.access_notes: Internal midshipman event; no public participation is implied.

cards.title: Mark the Seven-Year Commitment
cards.subtitle: Officer-professionalism program ceremony
cards.notes: Read the current Academy instruction for the ceremony’s purpose and keep it in its formal service-commitment context rather than treating it as a public dinner.
cards.short_summary: A dinner recognizes class members who have formally committed to the next seven years.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA’s current professionalism and civility instruction states that the Commitment Dinner celebrates class members who have formally dedicated the next seven years.
cards.source_title: COMDTMIDNINST 1520.4D Professionalism and Civility Training Program
cards.access_notes: A midshipman program event; participation and attendance are determined by USNA.

cards.title: Send the Game Ball Down the Road
cards.subtitle: 13th Company Army–Navy relay tradition
cards.notes: Follow official Army–Navy coverage for this organized relay; do not join the route or interfere with runners, traffic control, or security operations.
cards.short_summary: 13th Company carries a game ball by relay in the lead-up to Army–Navy.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA states that the Army–Navy ball run began in 1982 and describes 13th Company’s traditional game-ball relay before the rivalry game.
cards.source_title: Naval Academy Gears Up for Army-Navy Football
cards.access_notes: The cited USNA notice says the ball run was not open to the general public; verify current arrangements before viewing.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at United States Naval Academy, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A conservative, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence combining Academy orientation with nearby public Annapolis landmarks. Confirm campus access and any event-specific restrictions before going.

cards.title: Start at the Visitor Center
cards.subtitle: Gate 1, United States Naval Academy
cards.notes: Use the Visitor Center as the practical starting point: pick up current visitor information and ask which Academy areas are accessible that day.
cards.short_summary: Begin with current on-site orientation and access information.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA Admissions identifies the Visitor Center at 52 King George Street and directs visitors there for Academy visits.
cards.access_notes: General public visitation resumed May 11, 2026, but Academy access is controlled; verify entry requirements before arrival.

cards.title: Attend an Admissions Briefing
cards.subtitle: Visitor Center, United States Naval Academy
cards.notes: If you are considering USNA, use the daily briefing to ground the weekend in official information before exploring the Yard and Annapolis.
cards.short_summary: Hear admissions information directly from USNA.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA states that daily in-person admissions briefings are available at 1000 and 1400.
cards.access_notes: USNA lists daily briefings at 1000 and 1400; confirm status before traveling.

cards.title: Take a Guided Yard Tour
cards.subtitle: Departing from the Visitor Center
cards.notes: Choose a scheduled guided tour if offered, then use it to learn the layout and history without assuming unrestricted access to campus spaces.
cards.short_summary: See the Yard through the official visitor-tour program.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA directs visitors to the Naval Academy Tourism website for available tours and ticket purchases.
cards.access_notes: Tour availability and access conditions can change; purchase or reserve only through the official tour provider.

cards.title: Browse Preble Hall Exhibits
cards.subtitle: Preble Hall, United States Naval Academy
cards.notes: Spend time with the ship models, artifacts, and seapower exhibits; the museum provides a focused introduction to Navy and Academy history.
cards.short_summary: Two floors of naval-history exhibits in Preble Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Naval Academy Museum is in Preble Hall and presents exhibits on seapower, the U.S. Navy, and the Academy.
cards.access_notes: Museum access depends on Academy entry conditions; its official page directs visitors to plan their visit.

cards.title: See the Academy Chapel
cards.subtitle: United States Naval Academy
cards.notes: When it is open for visitors, take a quiet look at the chapel’s architecture and remember that services and official events take priority.
cards.short_summary: A prominent Academy chapel with active religious use.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA’s chaplaincy describes the Brigade of Midshipmen Chapel as part of its chapel heritage and virtual-tour offerings.
cards.source_title: Virtual Chapel Tours | Chaplains Center | USNA
cards.access_notes: Visitor access may be limited by worship services, ceremonies, and Academy security; confirm on arrival.

cards.title: Visit the John Paul Jones Crypt
cards.subtitle: Brigade of Midshipmen Chapel, United States Naval Academy
cards.notes: Pair the crypt with the chapel stop and use the Academy’s interpretive material to understand its connection to naval history.
cards.short_summary: A named historic crypt within the Academy chapel complex.
cards.evidence_claim: USNA includes the Crypt of John Paul Jones among the chapel spaces presented in its virtual chapel tours.
cards.source_title: Virtual Chapel Tours | Chaplains Center | USNA
cards.access_notes: Access follows chapel and Academy visitor conditions; do not enter during services or private events.

cards.title: Step Inside the Maryland State House
cards.subtitle: 100 State Circle, Annapolis
cards.notes: Use the self-guided information on the first floor, allowing time for the required security screening and photo-ID check at entry.
cards.short_summary: A public historic building with self-guided material.
cards.evidence_claim: The Maryland State Archives says the State House is open to the public daily from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., except Christmas and New Year’s Day.
cards.access_notes: Photo ID and metal-detector screening are required; public hours are 8:30 a.m.–5:00 p.m. daily except Christmas and New Year’s Day.

cards.title: Read the City Dock Memorial
cards.subtitle: City Dock, historic Annapolis
cards.notes: Walk the sculpture group, Compass Rose, and Story Wall slowly; use the plaques as prompts for a thoughtful conversation about family history.
cards.short_summary: A three-part City Dock memorial centered on history and remembrance.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Annapolis describes the memorial as three areas: the Alex Haley sculpture group, Compass Rose, and Story Wall.
cards.access_notes: Located at City Dock; respect the memorial and any temporary event setup in the area.

cards.title: Pause at Susan Campbell Park
cards.subtitle: City Dock, Spa Creek, Annapolis
cards.notes: Make this a short waterfront reset: sit, look across Spa Creek, and note any civic programming without relying on an event being scheduled.
cards.short_summary: A waterfront civic space at City Dock.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Annapolis identifies Susan Campbell Park as its most visible waterfront park and civic space on Spa Creek.
cards.source_title: City of Annapolis Water Access Plan
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public space; conditions may be affected by weather, tides, or permitted events.

cards.title: Finish with the Park Campus Trails
cards.subtitle: 7300 Edgewood Road, Annapolis
cards.notes: Use the waterfront trails and public paddle-craft launch for a daylight outdoor finish; bring what you need and follow posted waterfront guidance.
cards.short_summary: A 12-acre waterfront park with trails and a public launch.
cards.evidence_claim: The Annapolis Maritime Museum & Park says its Park Campus is open daily dawn to dusk and includes hiking trails and a public paddle-craft launch.
cards.source_title: Visit 2025 | The Annapolis Maritime Museum & Park
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk according to the museum; use the trails and launch only in daylight and follow posted site guidance.

warnings: Campus access, tours, and chapel availability are subject to security procedures and official events; verify details immediately before visiting.
